evidence.fact: tlock 0.0.10; RFC9380 default enabled; HEAD 2026-07-13.
Low-level API handles only 16-byte keys; decrypt truncates trailing zero bytes.

Age wrapper checks header chain hash and restores the decrypted file key to 16 bytes, compensating for low-level zero truncation. It consumes a caller-supplied signature without verifying the requested round/key itself.

workaround: Use tlock_age rather than raw tlock for bids; externally verify the beacon signature against the exact pinned chain/key/round. Cross-test Go/TypeScript/Rust age interoperability including zero-ending keys; the wrapper padding means raw truncation alone is not evidence that age decryption fails.

evidence.fact: Default randomness chain is chained/30s and unsuitable for tlock; quicknet is unchained/3s, hash 52db9ba70e0cc0f6eaf7803dd07447a1f5477735fd3f661792ba94600c84e971, genesis 1692803367.

evidence.fact: Verifier checks requested round, SHA256(signature) randomness, then BLS against SHA256(uint64be(round)) with RFC9380 G1 DST.

workaround: Reject wrong chain/key/scheme/round, use verified signature as release key; choose first round at or after auction release UTC.

evidence.fact: Quicknet IBE key wrapper U in G2 (96 bytes) + V/W (16 each) = 128 bytes.
One stanza age header base64/wrap/MAC; derived raw length for an 8-digit round and nonempty payload below 64KiB is 359 + payload bytes.
Armor adds base64 and PEM-like header/footer; a one-byte payload gives about 554 bytes, already exceeding a memo. Raw-length formula applies to nonempty payloads.

workaround: Decode armor as binary bytes, prefix 0xFF; 128-byte payload gives 488 memo bytes. Maximum payload 152 bytes with no extra app envelope for an 8-digit round. For larger bids store fixed-size ciphertext off-chain and put version/auction-id/round/SHA256 digest in memo; do not use UTF-8 encoding of a binary JS string.
